gene.name: argonaute RISC catalytic component 2
gene.function: Required for RNA-mediated gene silencing (RNAi) by the RNA- induced silencing complex (RISC). The 'minimal RISC' appears to include AGO2 bound to a short guide RNA such as a microRNA (miRNA) or short interfering RNA (siRNA). These guide RNAs direct RISC to complementary mRNAs that are targets for RISC-mediated gene silencing. The precise mechanism of gene silencing depends on the degree of complementarity between the miRNA or siRNA and its target. Binding of RISC to a perfectly complementary mRNA generally results in silencing due to endonucleolytic cleavage of the mRNA specifically by AGO2. Binding of RISC to a partially complementary mRNA results in silencing through inhibition of translation, and this is independent of endonuclease activity. May inhibit translation initiation by binding to the 7- methylguanosine cap, thereby preventing the recruitment of the translation initiation factor eIF4-E. May also inhibit translation initiation via interaction with EIF6, which itself binds to the 60S ribosomal subunit and prevents its association with the 40S ribosomal subunit. The inhibition of translational initiation leads to the accumulation of the affected mRNA in cytoplasmic processing bodies (P- bodies), where mRNA degradation may subsequently occur. In some cases RISC-mediated translational repression is also observed for miRNAs that perfectly match the 3' untranslated region (3'-UTR). Can also up- regulate the translation of specific mRNAs under certain growth conditions. Binds to the AU element of the 3'-UTR of the TNF mRNA and up-regulates translation under conditions of serum starvation. Also required for transcriptional gene silencing (TGS), in which short RNAs known as antigene RNAs or agRNAs direct the transcriptional repression of complementary promoter regions.

gene.name: apolipoprotein B
gene.function: Apolipoprotein B is a major protein constituent of chylomicrons (apo B-48), LDL (apo B-100) and VLDL (apo B-100). Apo B- 100 functions as a recognition signal for the cellular binding and internalization of LDL particles by the apoB/E receptor.

gene.name: apolipoprotein E
gene.function: APOE is an apolipoprotein, a protein associating with lipid particles, that mainly functions in lipoprotein-mediated lipid transport between organs via the plasma and interstitial fluids. APOE is a core component of plasma lipoproteins and is involved in their production, conversion and clearance. Apolipoproteins are amphipathic molecules that interact both with lipids of the lipoprotein particle core and the aqueous environment of the plasma. As such, APOE associates with chylomicrons, chylomicron remnants, very low density lipoproteins (VLDL) and intermediate density lipoproteins (IDL) but shows a preferential binding to high-density lipoproteins (HDL). It also binds a wide range of cellular receptors including the LDL receptor/LDLR, the LDL receptor-related proteins LRP1, LRP2 and LRP8 and the very low-density lipoprotein receptor/VLDLR that mediate the cellular uptake of the APOE-containing lipoprotein particles. Finally, APOE also has a heparin-binding activity and binds heparan- sulfate proteoglycans on the surface of cells, a property that supports the capture and the receptor-mediated uptake of APOE-containing lipoproteins by cells. A main function of APOE is to mediate lipoprotein clearance through the uptake of chylomicrons, VLDLs, and HDLs by hepatocytes. APOE is also involved in the biosynthesis by the liver of VLDLs as well as their uptake by peripheral tissues ensuring the delivery of triglycerides and energy storage in muscle, heart and adipose tissues. By participating in the lipoprotein-mediated distribution of lipids among tissues, APOE plays a critical role in plasma and tissues lipid homeostasis. APOE is also involved in two steps of reverse cholesterol transport, the HDLs-mediated transport of cholesterol from peripheral tissues to the liver, and thereby plays an important role in cholesterol homeostasis. First, it is functionally associated with ABCA1 in the biogenesis of HDLs in tissues. Second, it is enriched in circulating HDLs and mediates their uptake by hepatocytes. APOE also plays an important role in lipid transport in the central nervous system, regulating neuron survival and sprouting. APOE is also involved in innate and adaptive immune responses, controlling for instance the survival of myeloid-derived suppressor cells (By similarity). Binds to the immune cell receptor LILRB4. APOE may also play a role in transcription regulation through a receptor-dependent and cholesterol-independent mechanism, that activates MAP3K12 and a non-canonical MAPK signal transduction pathway that results in enhanced AP-1-mediated transcription of APP.

gene.name: DnaJ heat shock protein family (Hsp40) member B1
gene.function: Interacts with HSP70 and can stimulate its ATPase activity. Acts also with TTC1 as a chaperone adapter that regulates HSP70- dependent folding process by interacting with the HSP70 amino terminal region. Stimulates the association between HSC70 and HIP. Negatively regulates heat shock-induced HSF1 transcriptional activity during the attenuation and recovery phase period of the heat shock response. Stimulates ATP hydrolysis and the folding of unfolded proteins mediated by HSPA1A/B (in vitro).

gene.name: hydroxysteroid 17-beta dehydrogenase 13
gene.function: Plays a pivotal role in hepatic lipid metabolism. In vitro, it catalyzes the oxidation of a variety of lipid substrates, including 17beta-estradiol, retinol, retinal, and leukotriene B4.

gene.name: heat shock protein family A (Hsp70) member 8
gene.function: Molecular chaperone implicated in a wide variety of cellular processes, including protection of the proteome from stress, folding and transport of newly synthesized polypeptides, chaperone-mediated autophagy, activation of proteolysis of misfolded proteins, formation and dissociation of protein complexes, and antigen presentation. Plays a pivotal role in the protein quality control system, ensuring the correct folding of proteins, the re-folding of misfolded proteins and controlling the targeting of proteins for subsequent degradation. This is achieved through cycles of ATP binding, ATP hydrolysis and ADP release, mediated by co-chaperones. The co-chaperones have been shown to not only regulate different steps of the ATPase cycle of HSP70, but they also have an individual specificity such that one co-chaperone may promote folding of a substrate while another may promote degradation. The affinity of HSP70 for polypeptides is regulated by its nucleotide bound state. In the ATP-bound form, it has a low affinity for substrate proteins. However, upon hydrolysis of the ATP to ADP, it undergoes a conformational change that increases its affinity for substrate proteins. HSP70 goes through repeated cycles of ATP hydrolysis and nucleotide exchange, which permits cycles of substrate binding and release. The HSP70-associated co-chaperones are of three types: J- domain co-chaperones HSP40s (stimulate ATPase hydrolysis by HSP70), the nucleotide exchange factors (NEF) such as BAG1/2/3 (facilitate conversion of HSP70 from the ADP-bound to the ATP-bound state thereby promoting substrate release), and the TPR domain chaperones such as HOPX and STUB1. Plays a critical role in mitochondrial import, delivers preproteins to the mitochondrial import receptor TOMM70. Acts as a repressor of transcriptional activation. Inhibits the transcriptional coactivator activity of CITED1 on Smad- mediated transcription. Component of the PRP19-CDC5L complex that forms an integral part of the spliceosome and is required for activating pre- mRNA splicing. May have a scaffolding role in the spliceosome assembly as it contacts all other components of the core complex. Binds bacterial lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and mediates LPS-induced inflammatory response, including TNF secretion by monocytes. Substrate recognition component in chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA), a selective protein degradation process that mediates degradation of proteins with a -KFERQ motif: HSPA8/HSC70 specifically recognizes and binds cytosolic proteins bearing a -KFERQ motif and promotes their recruitment to the surface of the lysosome where they bind to lysosomal protein LAMP2. KFERQ motif- containing proteins are eventually transported into the lysosomal lumen where they are degraded. In conjunction with LAMP2, facilitates MHC class II presentation of cytoplasmic antigens by guiding antigens to the lysosomal membrane for interaction with LAMP2 which then elicits MHC class II presentation of peptides to the cell membrane. Participates in the ER-associated degradation (ERAD) quality control pathway in conjunction with J domain-containing co- chaperones and the E3 ligase STUB1. It is recruited to clathrin-coated vesicles through its interaction with DNAJC6 leading to activation of HSPA8/HSC70 ATPase activity and therefore uncoating of clathrin-coated vesicles (By similarity).

gene.name: islet amyloid polypeptide
gene.function: Amylin/IAPP is a glucoregulatory peptide hormone that plays an important role in the regulation of energy homeostasis. Selectively inhibits insulin-stimulated glucose utilization and glycogen deposition in muscle, while not affecting adipocyte glucose metabolism. IAPP function is mediated by the CALCR- RAMPs (AMYRs) receptor complexes (By similarity). Amylin can also bind CALCR receptor in the absence of RAMPs, although it is more selective for AMYRs (By similarity).

gene.name: integral membrane protein 2B
gene.function: Plays a regulatory role in the processing of the amyloid-beta A4 precursor protein (APP) and acts as an inhibitor of the amyloid-beta peptide aggregation and fibrils deposition. Plays a role in the induction of neurite outgrowth. Functions as a protease inhibitor by blocking access of secretases to APP cleavage sites.

gene.name: microtubule associated protein tau
gene.function: Promotes microtubule assembly and stability, and might be involved in the establishment and maintenance of neuronal polarity. The C-terminus binds axonal microtubules while the N-terminus binds neural plasma membrane components, suggesting that tau functions as a linker protein between both. Axonal polarity is predetermined by TAU/MAPT localization (in the neuronal cell) in the domain of the cell body defined by the centrosome. The short isoforms allow plasticity of the cytoskeleton whereas the longer isoforms may preferentially play a role in its stabilization.

gene.name: multivesicular body subunit 12A
gene.function: Component of the ESCRT-I complex, a regulator of vesicular trafficking process. Required for the sorting of endocytic ubiquitinated cargos into multivesicular bodies. May be involved in the ligand-mediated internalization and down-regulation of EGF receptor. .

gene.name: sirtuin 1
gene.function: NAD-dependent protein deacetylase that links transcriptional regulation directly to intracellular energetics and participates in the coordination of several separated cellular functions such as cell cycle, response to DNA damage, metabolism, apoptosis and autophagy. Can modulate chromatin function through deacetylation of histones and can promote alterations in the methylation of histones and DNA, leading to transcriptional repression. Deacetylates a broad range of transcription factors and coregulators, thereby regulating target gene expression positively and negatively. Serves as a sensor of the cytosolic ratio of NAD(+)/NADH which is altered by glucose deprivation and metabolic changes associated with caloric restriction. Is essential in skeletal muscle cell differentiation and in response to low nutrients mediates the inhibitory effect on skeletal myoblast differentiation which also involves 5'-AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT) (By similarity). Component of the eNoSC (energy-dependent nucleolar silencing) complex, a complex that mediates silencing of rDNA in response to intracellular energy status and acts by recruiting histone-modifying enzymes. The eNoSC complex is able to sense the energy status of cell: upon glucose starvation, elevation of NAD(+)/NADP(+) ratio activates SIRT1, leading to histone H3 deacetylation followed by dimethylation of H3 at 'Lys-9' (H3K9me2) by SUV39H1 and the formation of silent chromatin in the rDNA locus. Deacetylates 'Lys-266' of SUV39H1, leading to its activation. Inhibits skeletal muscle differentiation by deacetylating PCAF and MYOD1. Deacetylates H2A and 'Lys-26' of H1-4. Deacetylates 'Lys-16' of histone H4 (in vitro). Involved in NR0B2/SHP corepression function through chromatin remodeling: Recruited to LRH1 target gene promoters by NR0B2/SHP thereby stimulating histone H3 and H4 deacetylation leading to transcriptional repression. Proposed to contribute to genomic integrity via positive regulation of telomere length; however, reports on localization to pericentromeric heterochromatin are conflicting (By similarity). Proposed to play a role in constitutive heterochromatin (CH) formation and/or maintenance through regulation of the available pool of nuclear SUV39H1. Upon oxidative/metabolic stress decreases SUV39H1 degradation by inhibiting SUV39H1 polyubiquitination by MDM2. This increase in SUV39H1 levels enhances SUV39H1 turnover in CH, which in turn seems to accelerate renewal of the heterochromatin which correlates with greater genomic integrity during stress response. Deacetylates 'Lys-382' of p53/TP53 and impairs its ability to induce transcription-dependent proapoptotic program and modulate cell senescence. Deacetylates TAF1B and thereby represses rDNA transcription by the RNA polymerase I (By similarity). Deacetylates MYC, promotes the association of MYC with MAX and decreases MYC stability leading to compromised transformational capability. Deacetylates FOXO3 in response to oxidative stress thereby increasing its ability to induce cell cycle arrest and resistance to oxidative stress but inhibiting FOXO3-mediated induction of apoptosis transcriptional activity; also leading to FOXO3 ubiquitination and protesomal degradation. Appears to have a similar effect on MLLT7/FOXO4 in regulation of transcriptional activity and apoptosis. Deacetylates DNMT1; thereby impairs DNMT1 methyltransferase-independent transcription repressor activity, modulates DNMT1 cell cycle regulatory function and DNMT1-mediated gene silencing. Deacetylates RELA/NF-kappa-B p65 thereby inhibiting its transactivating potential and augments apoptosis in response to TNF. Deacetylates HIF1A, KAT5/TIP60, RB1 and HIC1. Deacetylates FOXO1 resulting in its nuclear retention and enhancement of its transcriptional activity leading to increased gluconeogenesis in liver. Inhibits E2F1 transcriptional activity and apoptotic function, possibly by deacetylation. Involved in HES1- and HEY2-mediated transcriptional repression. In cooperation with MYCN seems to be involved in transcriptional repression of DUSP6/MAPK3 leading to MYCN stabilization by phosphorylation at 'Ser-62'. Deacetylates MEF2D. Required for antagonist-mediated transcription suppression of AR-dependent genes which may be linked to local deacetylation of histone H3. Represses HNF1A-mediated transcription (By similarity). Required for the repression of ESRRG by CREBZF. Deacetylates NR1H3 and NR1H2 and deacetylation of NR1H3 at 'Lys-434' positively regulates transcription of NR1H3:RXR target genes, promotes NR1H3 proteasomal degradation and results in cholesterol efflux; a promoter clearing mechanism after reach round of transcription is proposed. Involved in lipid metabolism: deacetylates LPIN1, thereby inhibiting diacylglycerol synthesis. Implicated in regulation of adipogenesis and fat mobilization in white adipocytes by repression of PPARG which probably involves association with NCOR1 and SMRT/NCOR2 (By similarity). Deacetylates p300/EP300 and PRMT1 (By similarity). Deacetylates ACSS2 leading to its activation, and HMGCS1 deacetylation. Involved in liver and muscle metabolism. Through deacetylation and activation of PPARGC1A is required to activate fatty acid oxidation in skeletal muscle under low-glucose conditions and is involved in glucose homeostasis. Involved in regulation of PPARA and fatty acid beta-oxidation in liver. Involved in positive regulation of insulin secretion in pancreatic beta cells in response to glucose; the function seems to imply transcriptional repression of UCP2. Proposed to deacetylate IRS2 thereby facilitating its insulin-induced tyrosine phosphorylation. Deacetylates SREBF1 isoform SREBP-1C thereby decreasing its stability and transactivation in lipogenic gene expression. Involved in DNA damage response by repressing genes which are involved in DNA repair, such as XPC and TP73, deacetylating XRCC6/Ku70, and facilitating recruitment of additional factors to sites of damaged DNA, such as SIRT1-deacetylated NBN can recruit ATM to initiate DNA repair and SIRT1-deacetylated XPA interacts with RPA2. Also involved in DNA repair of DNA double-strand breaks by homologous recombination and specifically single-strand annealing independently of XRCC6/Ku70 and NBN. Promotes DNA double-strand breaks by mediating deacetylation of SIRT6. Transcriptional suppression of XPC probably involves an E2F4:RBL2 suppressor complex and protein kinase B (AKT) signaling. Transcriptional suppression of TP73 probably involves E2F4 and PCAF. Deacetylates WRN thereby regulating its helicase and exonuclease activities and regulates WRN nuclear translocation in response to DNA damage. Deacetylates APEX1 at 'Lys-6' and 'Lys-7' and stimulates cellular AP endonuclease activity by promoting the association of APEX1 to XRCC1. Catalyzes deacetylation of ERCC4/XPF, thereby impairing interaction with ERCC1 and nucleotide excision repair (NER). Increases p53/TP53-mediated transcription- independent apoptosis by blocking nuclear translocation of cytoplasmic p53/TP53 and probably redirecting it to mitochondria. Deacetylates XRCC6/Ku70 at 'Lys-539' and 'Lys-542' causing it to sequester BAX away from mitochondria thereby inhibiting stress-induced apoptosis. Is involved in autophagy, presumably by deacetylating ATG5, ATG7 and MAP1LC3B/ATG8. Deacetylates AKT1 which leads to enhanced binding of AKT1 and PDK1 to PIP3 and promotes their activation. Acts as a regulator of AMPK activity in response to calorie restriction: deacetylates the ATP6V1E1 subunit of the V-ATPase complex following activation by TULP3, leading to (1) V-ATPase complex inhibition on lysosomes and (2) AMPK activation via the AXIN1- STK11/LKB1 axis (By similarity). Proposed to play role in regulation of STK11/LBK1-dependent AMPK signaling pathways implicated in cellular senescence which seems to involve the regulation of the acetylation status of STK11/LBK1. Can deacetylate STK11/LBK1 and thereby increase its activity, cytoplasmic localization and association with STRAD; however, the relevance of such activity in normal cells is unclear. In endothelial cells is shown to inhibit STK11/LBK1 activity and to promote its degradation. Deacetylates SMAD7 at 'Lys-64' and 'Lys-70' thereby promoting its degradation. Deacetylates CIITA and augments its MHC class II transactivation and contributes to its stability. Deacetylates MECOM/EVI1. Deacetylates PML at 'Lys- 487' and this deacetylation promotes PML control of PER2 nuclear localization. During the neurogenic transition, represses selective NOTCH1-target genes through histone deacetylation in a BCL6-dependent manner and leading to neuronal differentiation. Regulates the circadian expression of several core clock genes, including BMAL1, RORC, PER2 and CRY1 and plays a critical role in maintaining a controlled rhythmicity in histone acetylation, thereby contributing to circadian chromatin remodeling. Deacetylates BMAL1 and histones at the circadian gene promoters in order to facilitate repression by inhibitory components of the circadian oscillator (By similarity). Deacetylates PER2, facilitating its ubiquitination and degradation by the proteasome (By similarity). Protects cardiomyocytes against palmitate-induced apoptosis (By similarity). Deacetylates XBP1 isoform 2; deacetylation decreases protein stability of XBP1 isoform 2 and inhibits its transcriptional activity. Deacetylates PCK1 and directs its activity toward phosphoenolpyruvate production promoting gluconeogenesis. Involved in the CCAR2-mediated regulation of PCK1 and NR1D1. Deacetylates CTNB1 at 'Lys-49'. In POMC (pro-opiomelanocortin) neurons, required for leptin-induced activation of PI3K signaling (By similarity). Deacetylates SOX9; promoting SOX9 nuclear localization and transactivation activity (By similarity). Involved in the regulation of centrosome duplication: deacetylates CENATAC in G1 phase, allowing for SASS6 accumulation on the centrosome and subsequent procentriole assembly. Deacetylates NDC80/HEC1. In addition to protein deacetylase activity, also acts as a protein- lysine deacylase by mediating protein delactylation, depropionylation and decrotonylation. Mediates depropionylation of Osterix (SP7) (By similarity). Catalyzes decrotonylation of histones; it however does not represent a major histone decrotonylase. Mediates protein delactylation of TEAD1 and YAP1.

gene.name: solute carrier family 2 member 2
gene.function: Facilitative hexose transporter that mediates the transport of glucose, fructose and galactose. Likely mediates the bidirectional transfer of glucose across the plasma membrane of hepatocytes and is responsible for uptake of glucose by the beta cells; may comprise part of the glucose-sensing mechanism of beta cells. May also participate with the Na(+)/glucose cotransporter in the transcellular transport of glucose in the small intestine and kidney. Also able to mediate the transport of dehydroascorbate and urate.

gene.name: small RNA binding exonuclease protection factor La
gene.function: Binds to the 3' poly(U) terminus of nascent RNA polymerase III transcripts, protecting them from exonuclease digestion and facilitating their folding and maturation. In case of Coxsackievirus B3 infection, binds to the viral internal ribosome entry site (IRES) and stimulates the IRES- mediated translation.

gene.name: toll like receptor 4
gene.function: Transmembrane receptor that functions as a pattern recognition receptor recognizing pathogen- and damage-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs and DAMPs) to induce innate immune responses via downstream signaling pathways. At the plasma membrane, cooperates with LY96 to mediate the innate immune response to bacterial lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Also involved in LPS- independent inflammatory responses triggered by free fatty acids, such as palmitate, and Ni(2+). Mechanistically, acts via MYD88, TIRAP and TRAF6, leading to NF-kappa-B activation, cytokine secretion and the inflammatory response. Alternatively, CD14-mediated TLR4 internalization via endocytosis is associated with the initiation of a MYD88-independent signaling via the TICAM1-TBK1-IRF3 axis leading to type I interferon production. In addition to the secretion of proinflammatory cytokines, initiates the activation of NLRP3 inflammasome and formation of a positive feedback loop between autophagy and NF-kappa-B signaling cascade. In complex with TLR6, promotes inflammation in monocytes/macrophages by associating with TLR6 and the receptor CD86. Upon ligand binding, such as oxLDL or amyloid-beta 42, the TLR4:TLR6 complex is internalized and triggers inflammatory response, leading to NF-kappa-B-dependent production of CXCL1, CXCL2 and CCL9 cytokines, via MYD88 signaling pathway, and CCL5 cytokine, via TICAM1 signaling pathway. In myeloid dendritic cells, vesicular stomatitis virus glycoprotein G but not LPS promotes the activation of IRF7, leading to type I IFN production in a CD14- dependent manner. Required for the migration-promoting effects of ZG16B/PAUF on pancreatic cancer cells.

gene.name: tumor susceptibility 101
gene.function: Component of the ESCRT-I complex, a regulator of vesicular trafficking process. Binds to ubiquitinated cargo proteins and is required for the sorting of endocytic ubiquitinated cargos into multivesicular bodies (MVBs). Mediates the association between the ESCRT-0 and ESCRT-I complex. Required for completion of cytokinesis; the function requires CEP55. May be involved in cell growth and differentiation. Acts as a negative growth regulator. Involved in the budding of many viruses through an interaction with viral proteins that contain a late-budding motif P-[ST]-A-P. This interaction is essential for viral particle budding of numerous retroviruses. Required for the exosomal release of SDCBP, CD63 and syndecan. It may also play a role in the extracellular release of microvesicles that differ from the exosomes.

gene.name: transthyretin
gene.function: Thyroid hormone-binding protein. Probably transports thyroxine from the bloodstream to the brain. .

gene.name: very low density lipoprotein receptor
gene.function: Multifunctional cell surface receptor that binds VLDL and transports it into cells by endocytosis and therefore plays an important role in energy metabolism. Also binds to a wide range of other molecules including Reelin/RELN or apolipoprotein E/APOE- containing ligands as well as clusterin/CLU. In the off-state of the pathway, forms homooligomers or heterooligomers with LRP8. Upon binding to ligands, homooligomers are rearranged to higher order receptor clusters that transmit the extracellular RELN signal to intracellular signaling processes by binding to DAB1. This interaction results in phosphorylation of DAB1 leading to the ultimate cell responses required for the correct positioning of newly generated neurons. Later, mediates a stop signal for migrating neurons, preventing them from entering the marginal zone (By similarity).

gene.name: VPS28 subunit of ESCRT-I
gene.function: Component of the ESCRT-I complex, a regulator of vesicular trafficking process. .

gene.name: VPS37A subunit of ESCRT-I
gene.function: Component of the ESCRT-I complex, a regulator of vesicular trafficking process. Required for the sorting of endocytic ubiquitinated cargos into multivesicular bodies. May be involved in cell growth and differentiation. .

phenotype.definition: Any cardiac rhythm other than the normal sinus rhythm. Such a rhythm may be either of sinus or ectopic origin and either regular or irregular. An arrhythmia may be due to a disturbance in impulse formation or conduction or both.

An atrial arrhythmia characterized by disorganized atrial activity without discrete P waves on the surface EKG, but instead by an undulating baseline or more sharply circumscribed atrial deflections of varying amplitude an frequency ranging from 350 to 600 per minute.
phenotype.lay: Quivering upper heart chambers resulting in irregular heartbeat

phenotype.definition: Block of conduction of electrical impulses along the Bundle of His or along one of its bundle branches.

Extracellular deposition in cardiac tissue of a proteinaceous material that, when stained with Congo red, demonstrates apple-green birefringence under polarized light and that has a distinct color when stained with sulfated Alcian blue. Viewed with electron microscopy, the amyloid deposits are seen to be composed of a beta-sheet fibrillar material. These nonbranching fibrils have a diameter of 7.5 to 10 nm and are the result of protein misfolding.
A type of cardiac amyloidosis related to deposition of transthyretin (TTR), which is identified by immunohistochemical staining.

A myocardial disorder in which the heart muscle is structurally and functionally abnormal, in the absence of coronary artery disease, hypertension, valvular disease and congenital heart disease sufficient to cause the observed myocardial abnormality.
Amyloid deposition in the walls of leptomeningeal and cortical arteries, arterioles, and less often capillaries and veins of the central nervous system.
Difficulty in swallowing.
A multidimensional but common male sexual dysfunction that involves an alteration in any of the components of the erectile response, including organic, relational and psychological.
Inflammation of the renal glomeruli.
Steatosis is a term used to denote lipid accumulation within hepatocytes.
Enlargement or increased size of the heart left ventricle.
Increased length and width of the tongue.
A nonspecific term referring to disease or damage of the kidneys.

Neuropathic pain is triggered by lesions to the somatosensory nervous system that alter its structure and function so that pain occurs spontaneously and responses to noxious and innocuous stimuli are pathologically amplified.
A form of hypotension characterized by a sudden fall in blood pressure that occurs when a person assumes a standing position.
phenotype.lay: Decrease in blood pressure upon standing up

phenotype.definition: An unpleasant sensory and emotional experience associated with actual or potential tissue damage, or described in terms of such damage.
Abnormal sensations such as tingling, pricking, or numbness of the skin with no apparent physical cause.
Accumulation of fluid within the pericardium.

Peripheral neuropathy is a general term for any disorder of the peripheral nervous system. The main clinical features used to classify peripheral neuropathy are distribution, type (mainly demyelinating versus mainly axonal), duration, and course.
A generalized disorder of peripheral nerves.

Restrictive left ventricular physiology is characterized by a pattern of ventricular filling in which increased stiffness of the myocardium causes ventricular pressure to rise precipitously with only small increases in volume, defined as restrictive ventricular physiology in the presence of normal or reduced diastolic volumes (of one or both ventricles), normal or reduced systolic volumes, and normal ventricular wall thickness.
Peripheral neuropathy affecting the sensory nerves.
phenotype.lay: Damage to nerves that sense feeling

phenotype.definition: A transient loss of consciousness (i.e., characterized by a rapid onset, a short duration, and a spontaneous and complete recovery) due to cerebral hypoperfusion.
Weakness of all four limbs.
A reduction in the number of circulating thrombocytes.

gaps.experiment: Run a phase I dose-escalation study measuring liver TTR knockdown, plasma and tissue pharmacokinetics, adverse events, and hepatic safety before evaluating clinical benefit.

papers.title: Long-term effects of tafamidis for the treatment of transthyretin familial amyloid polyneuropathy.
papers.summary: In patients with Val30Met transthyretin familial amyloid polyneuropathy, tafamidis was generally well tolerated over 30 months, stabilized plasma TTR in approximately 94% of patients, and sustained or improved preservation of neurologic function, quality of life, and modified body mass index. Benefits were greater with earlier treatment, although the open-label extension, selected population, treatment interruptions, and absence of a continuous 30-month placebo group limit causal and long-term comparative conclusions.
papers.why: Long-term clinical data show that tafamidis stabilizes TTR and slows neurologic deterioration in hereditary transthyretin amyloid polyneuropathy.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of patisiran for familial amyloidotic polyneuropathy: a phase II multi-dose study.
papers.summary: In a phase II clinical study of 29 patients with transthyretin-mediated familial amyloid polyneuropathy, intravenous patisiran produced rapid, dose-dependent and durable reductions in serum TTR protein, reducing both mutant and wild-type TTR in Val30Met patients. The 0.3 mg/kg every-3-week regimen produced mean knockdown exceeding 85% after the second dose and a maximum of 96%, with generally mild-to-moderate adverse events, although infusion-related reactions and serious adverse events occurred.
papers.why: This phase II study in familial amyloidotic polyneuropathy shows dose-dependent patisiran-mediated knockdown of mutant and wild-type TTR with acceptable tolerability.

papers.title: Expert consensus recommendations to improve diagnosis of ATTR amyloidosis with polyneuropathy.
papers.summary: This consensus review concludes that hereditary ATTR amyloidosis with polyneuropathy is an underrecognized, genetically driven, systemic disorder with variable phenotypes and frequent diagnostic delay. It recommends TTR sequencing, tissue biopsy with Congo red staining and amyloid typing, selected bone-scintigraphy approaches, and multidisciplinary longitudinal assessment to diagnose the disease and identify multiorgan involvement early.
papers.why: The consensus recommendations provide a reusable diagnostic algorithm based on clinical red flags, TTR testing, biopsy, amyloid typing, and longitudinal monitoring for ATTR polyneuropathy.

papers.title: Impact of Earlier Diagnosis in Cardiac ATTR Amyloidosis Over the Course of 20 Years.
papers.summary: In a 20-year national-center cohort, patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis were increasingly detected earlier and at milder cardiac stages, alongside improved survival that persisted after censoring at the start of trials or disease-modifying therapy. The study also characterizes genotype-specific prognosis and the diagnostic pathways that enabled earlier recognition, while finding no age-adjusted survival benefit from diflunisal.
papers.why: A large longitudinal cohort shows that advanced cardiac imaging enables earlier ATTR cardiac amyloidosis diagnosis and quantifies its association with lower mortality.

papers.title: A Review of Patisiran (ONPATTRO®) for the Treatment of Polyneuropathy in People with Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis.
papers.summary: This review concludes that patisiran, a hepatocyte-directed siRNA therapeutic, lowers circulating wild-type and mutant TTR and improves polyneuropathy, autonomic function, quality of life, walking, and selected cardiac measures in adults with hereditary variant transthyretin amyloidosis. Its clinical benefits were not uniform: overall cardiac failure and serious cardiac adverse-event rates were similar to placebo, efficacy was not established in several excluded populations, and long-term use reduced vitamin A levels.
papers.why: The review summarizes a targeted gene-silencing therapy that reduces TTR production and improves neuropathy or cardiac outcomes in hereditary ATTR amyloidosis.

papers.title: Evolving landscape in the management of transthyretin amyloidosis.
papers.summary: This review describes hereditary ATTR amyloidosis as a TTR-variant-driven, multisystemic amyloid disorder and summarizes approaches that stabilize TTR, suppress TTR production, or clear amyloid deposits. Clinical evidence supports liver transplantation and tafamidis or diflunisal in selected early-stage polyneuropathy, while patisiran, revusiran, ISIS-TTRRx, doxycycline plus tauroursodeoxycholic acid, and amyloid-directed approaches remain investigational or have limited evidence.
papers.why: This review summarizes multiple clinically tested or investigational disease-modifying approaches for ATTR amyloidosis, including TTR stabilizers, gene-silencing therapies, amyloid disruption, and transplantation.

papers.title: Genotype-phenotype correlation and course of transthyretin familial amyloid polyneuropathies in France.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study shows strong genotype–phenotype heterogeneity in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis: Ile107Val, late-onset Val30Met, and Ser77Tyr forms had more rapid progression, severe axonal loss, frequent demyelinating findings, and more cardiac involvement than the Portuguese early-onset Val30Met group. The findings also highlight diagnostic challenges and describe liver transplantation, TTR-stabilizing drugs, RNA-silencing approaches, and anti–serum amyloid P antibodies as therapeutic strategies.
papers.why: Longitudinal genotype-specific cohorts provide natural-history endpoints and progression measures for TTR familial amyloid polyneuropathies that can support trial design.

papers.title: Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis.
papers.summary: This review describes transthyretin amyloidogenesis, the cardiac and neurologic phenotypes of hereditary ATTR amyloidosis, non-invasive diagnostic strategies, and disease-modifying approaches. It reports that TTR stabilizers, TTR gene-silencing agents, and an experimental in-vivo gene-editing therapy can reduce TTR production or stabilize TTR, while several imaging and serum biomarkers support diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring.
papers.why: The review describes noninvasive ATTR cardiac diagnosis, prognostic biomarkers, treatment-response imaging, and effective therapies applicable to variant hereditary ATTR disease.

papers.title: Repositioning tolcapone as a potent inhibitor of transthyretin amyloidogenesis and associated cellular toxicity.
papers.summary: The paper repurposes tolcapone as a potent transthyretin tetramer stabilizer and amyloidogenesis inhibitor, with stronger activity than tafamidis across wild-type and disease-associated TTR variants. Tolcapone stabilized TTR in human plasma ex vivo and after oral administration in humans, reduced TTR aggregation in several cellular systems, and protected against TTR-induced cardiac and Schwann-cell toxicity, but its short plasma half-life is a limitation.
papers.why: Tolcapone is shown in biochemical, structural, animal, and human-plasma experiments to bind and stabilize TTR and inhibit amyloidogenesis.

papers.title: Trial design and rationale for APOLLO, a Phase 3, placebo-controlled study of patisiran in patients with hereditary ATTR amyloidosis with polyneuropathy.
papers.summary: This trial-design paper describes APOLLO, a Phase 3 study evaluating patisiran for hereditary ATTR amyloidosis with polyneuropathy, and provides prior Phase 2 evidence that patisiran substantially reduces serum wild-type and mutant TTR. It also reviews liver transplantation, tafamidis, and diflunisal as approaches that can slow disease progression, while describing neurologic, autonomic, quality-of-life, cardiac, nerve-fiber, amyloid-burden, and pharmacodynamic outcome measures.
papers.why: The APOLLO trial design evaluates a patisiran RNAi treatment and provides disease-specific efficacy, safety, and multisystem outcome measures for hereditary ATTR polyneuropathy.

papers.title: Conventional heart failure therapy in cardiac ATTR amyloidosis.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 2371 patients with ATTR cardiac amyloidosis, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists were associated with lower mortality overall and in patients with LVEF >40%, while low-dose beta-blockers were associated with lower mortality in patients with LVEF ≤40%; ACE inhibitors/ARBs showed no convincing mortality association. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating, and the paper also summarizes tafamidis as a disease-specific therapy that stabilizes circulating transthyretin.
papers.why: This large observational study provides outcome data for conventional heart-failure therapies in cardiac ATTR amyloidosis and identifies mortality-associated treatment patterns.

papers.title: ATTR Amyloidosis: Current and Emerging Management Strategies: JACC: CardioOncology State-of-the-Art Review.
papers.summary: This review reports established transthyretin-stabilizing therapies and TTR gene-silencing strategies that improve clinical, neurophysiologic, functional, or cardiac outcomes in hereditary ATTR amyloidosis, while noting important adverse effects, advanced-stage limitations, and high costs. It also identifies noninvasive imaging and TTR- or neurofilament-associated biomarkers as promising research tools for subclinical disease, but emphasizes that validated screening and monitoring criteria remain absent.
papers.why: This same-disease review summarizes established and emerging treatments, monitoring strategies, and management approaches for ATTR cardiac amyloidosis.

papers.title: Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis in continental Western Europe: an insight through the Transthyretin Amyloidosis Outcomes Survey (THAOS).
papers.summary: The THAOS observational survey shows marked geographic, genotypic, and phenotypic heterogeneity among 1,411 symptomatic European patients with ATTR amyloidosis. Cardiac or mixed cardiac–neurologic phenotypes showed more severe echocardiographic abnormalities and lower survival than neurologic phenotypes, while electrocardiography, echocardiography, cardiac biomarkers, and TTR genetic testing supported recognition and differentiation of the disease.
papers.why: This paper reports an ongoing international longitudinal registry with data on hereditary and wild-type ATTR genotypes, phenotypes, cardiac involvement, and clinical recognition.

papers.title: Diagnosis and management of transthyretin familial amyloid polyneuropathy in Japan: red-flag symptom clusters and treatment algorithm.
papers.summary: This review consolidates the Japanese Val30Met ATTR-FAP landscape and proposes Japan-specific red-flag symptom clusters and a treatment algorithm. It identifies liver transplantation and TTR-stabilizing pharmacotherapy as disease-modifying options, while emphasizing limitations of transplantation, mixed clinical evidence for tafamidis and diflunisal, and the need for genetic, tissue, cardiac, and neurological confirmation.
papers.why: This paper develops a population-specific red-flag diagnostic cluster and treatment algorithm and summarizes liver transplantation and tafamidis for ATTR-FAP.

papers.title: In vivo detection of nerve injury in familial amyloid polyneuropathy by magnetic resonance neurography.
papers.summary: The study shows that high-resolution magnetic resonance neurography can detect, localize, and quantify lower-limb nerve injury in symptomatic transthyretin familial amyloid polyneuropathy, including injury in asymptomatic TTR mutation carriers before clinical or electrophysiological manifestations. Imaging identified a predominantly proximal thigh-level lesion burden, while proton spin density was elevated in both symptomatic patients and asymptomatic carriers and apparent T2 relaxation time distinguished symptomatic disease.
papers.why: Prospective patient data show that quantitative magnetic resonance neurography detects and localizes nerve injury in symptomatic and asymptomatic TTR mutation carriers.

papers.title: Patisiran Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics, and Exposure-Response Analyses in the Phase 3 APOLLO Trial in Patients With Hereditary Transthyretin-Mediated (hATTR) Amyloidosis.
papers.summary: In the phase 3 APOLLO trial, patisiran produced rapid, sustained, and substantial reductions in circulating transthyretin and improved neuropathy-related outcomes in patients with hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis. Its pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and safety effects were consistent across the evaluated patient subgroups, body weights, pharmacokinetic exposure ranges, and transient antidrug-antibody status, supporting 0.3 mg/kg every 3 weeks with a 30 mg maximum.
papers.why: The phase 3 APOLLO analysis establishes patisiran dosing, TTR lowering, exposure-response relationships, safety, and neurological efficacy in hATTR amyloidosis.

papers.title: (99m)Tc-DPD uptake reflects amyloid fibril composition in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis.
papers.summary: The paper shows a strong association between amyloid fibril composition and cardiac 99mTc-DPD scintigraphy in hereditary ATTR amyloidosis: type A fibrils containing truncated transthyretin were almost always 99mTc-DPD-positive, whereas type B fibrils containing only full-length transthyretin were consistently negative. Type A fibrils were associated with older age, greater cardiac hypertrophy, lower left ventricular ejection fraction, higher cardiac biomarker levels, and more cardiac abnormalities, although the study lacked cardiac biopsies in most scintigraphy-negative patients.
papers.why: The study validates Tc-99m DPD uptake as an assay strongly associated with ATTR amyloid fibril composition and evaluates alternative cardiac assessments.

papers.title: Preclinical evaluation of RNAi as a treatment for transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis.
papers.summary: The paper shows that liver-directed RNAi targeting TTR reduces hepatic TTR expression and circulating TTR, inhibits new deposition, and promotes regression of existing TTR deposits in hTTR V30M HSF1± mice. In comparative experiments, RNAi-mediated knockdown produced broader tissue deposit regression than tafamidis-mediated tetramer stabilization, while patisiran and revusiran showed durable serum TTR knockdown in cynomolgus monkeys.
papers.why: The study directly demonstrates that hepatic TTR knockdown with siRNA reduces and regresses TTR deposits in a mouse model of hereditary ATTR amyloidosis.

papers.title: Recommendations for presymptomatic genetic testing and management of individuals at risk for hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis.
papers.summary: This review recommends presymptomatic TTR genetic testing, multidisciplinary genetic counselling, and structured surveillance of asymptomatic TTR variant carriers to enable early diagnosis and timely treatment of TTR familial amyloid polyneuropathy. It emphasizes that tafamidis and selected liver transplantation have a limited treatment window, while small-fiber neurophysiology, cardiac testing, renal assessment, and selected MRI may improve detection of early disease.
papers.why: The ATTReuNET recommendations provide a concrete presymptomatic testing and longitudinal monitoring protocol for mutation carriers at risk of hereditary ATTR.

papers.title: Amyloid Deposits and Fibrosis on Left Ventricular Endomyocardial Biopsy Correlate With Extracellular Volume in Cardiac Amyloidosis.
papers.summary: In a 37-patient cardiac amyloidosis cohort, left ventricular endomyocardial biopsy showed that myocardial extracellular volume expansion was attributable to both amyloid deposits and nonoverlapping fibrosis, rather than amyloid alone. Their combined extent correlated with cardiac MRI extracellular volume, high-sensitivity troponin T, and NT-proBNP, although fibrosis alone did not correlate with extracellular volume and sST2 did not correlate with amyloid or collagen burden.
papers.why: The study directly links myocardial amyloid and fibrosis measurements to CMR extracellular volume and circulating biomarkers in transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis.

papers.title: Tc-99m labelled bone scintigraphy in suspected cardiac amyloidosis.
papers.summary: In a multinational retrospective cohort of 3,354 patients, the paper found that established non-biopsy diagnostic criteria were 97% specific for ATTR amyloid cardiomyopathy when used with refined serum free light chain ratio cut-offs, and all 403 biopsied patients meeting those criteria had ATTR amyloid. Radionuclide scintigraphy alone could neither establish ATTR amyloidosis nor exclude cardiac amyloidosis, while grade 1 uptake without monoclonal gammopathy strongly suggested ATTR amyloidosis.
papers.why: The large multicenter study validates and refines a noninvasive ATTR-CM diagnostic algorithm, including revised free light chain thresholds in chronic kidney disease.

papers.title: Phase 3 Multicenter Study of Revusiran in Patients with Hereditary Transthyretin-Mediated (hATTR) Amyloidosis with Cardiomyopathy (ENDEAVOUR).
papers.summary: The Phase 3 ENDEAVOUR trial found that revusiran produced sustained greater-than-80% reductions in serum TTR but did not improve ambulatory function, echocardiographic parameters, or cardiac biomarkers; an imbalanced mortality signal prompted termination, and its cause remained unidentified. The paper cites evidence from patisiran and proposes next-generation GalNAc–siRNA conjugates to further evaluate TTR lowering in ATTR cardiac amyloidosis.
papers.why: The phase 3 trial provides direct efficacy, pharmacodynamic, safety, and mortality data for revusiran in hATTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy, including a critical safety failure signal.

papers.title: Structural polymorphism of amyloid fibrils in ATTR amyloidosis revealed by cryo-electron microscopy.
papers.summary: Cryo-electron microscopy revealed that cardiac transthyretin amyloid fibrils from three patients carrying the ATTRv-I84S mutation have a common core but multiple patient-specific gate conformations, with different folds sometimes coexisting within one fibril. Mass spectrometry, fibril-seeding experiments, and in silico stability analyses indicate that the structural variation is associated with the mutation rather than differential proteolysis, while its relationships to disease progression and pathogenicity remain unresolved.
papers.why: The paper demonstrates a cryo-electron microscopy method for resolving distinct fibril structures directly in cardiac tissue from patients with ATTRv-I84S amyloidosis.

papers.title: Advances in the treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis: A review.
papers.summary: This review reports that hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis is driven by amyloidogenic transthyretin and describes diagnostic procedures, established treatments, and investigational agents. TTR gene-silencing therapies inotersen and patisiran substantially lower TTR and improve or stabilize neuropathy, while tafamidis improves cardiomyopathy outcomes but has mixed efficacy across neuropathy stages and genotypes; liver transplantation, diflunisal, and experimental TTR-directed agents have important efficacy and safety limitations.
papers.why: The review consolidates clinical evidence for multiple existing treatments of hereditary ATTR amyloidosis, including gene-silencing drugs, stabilizers, and transplantation.

papers.title: Clinical and genetic profile of patients enrolled in the Transthyretin Amyloidosis Outcomes Survey (THAOS): 14-year update.
papers.summary: The 14-year THAOS analysis of more than 5,000 symptomatic patients and asymptomatic carriers demonstrates marked genotypic, regional, and phenotypic heterogeneity in ATTR amyloidosis, including substantial mixed and multisystem disease. The paper also identifies clinical outcome measures, diagnostic approaches, comprehensive multidisciplinary assessment, and recently approved disease-modifying therapy classes relevant to further research and earlier intervention.
papers.why: THAOS is an ongoing global registry and longitudinal cohort resource containing symptomatic ATTR patients and asymptomatic TTR mutation carriers.

papers.title: Inotersen: new promise for the treatment of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis.
papers.summary: This review identifies inotersen as an antisense oligonucleotide that reduces hepatic production of both mutant and wild-type transthyretin through RNase H1-mediated degradation of TTR mRNA. Clinical studies reported reduced neuropathy progression and improved quality of life in hereditary ATTR polyneuropathy, although thrombocytopenia, glomerulonephritis, and lack of retinal or leptomeningeal efficacy remain important limitations.
papers.why: The paper reports Phase III evidence that RNase H-mediated TTR suppression with inotersen improves disease course and quality of life in hereditary polyneuropathy.

papers.title: A 15-year consolidated overview of data in over 6000 patients from the Transthyretin Amyloidosis Outcomes Survey (THAOS).
papers.summary: This 15-year analysis of the Transthyretin Amyloidosis Outcomes Survey describes clinical, genotypic, phenotypic, neurologic, cardiac, gastrointestinal, and quality-of-life heterogeneity among 4428 symptomatic patients and 1707 asymptomatic TTR mutation carriers. It found marked regional and genotype-dependent differences in disease presentation, with V30M-associated disease commonly showing neurologic and gastrointestinal manifestations and wild-type disease showing greater cardiac involvement; no therapeutic efficacy results were reported.
papers.why: THAOS is a large global longitudinal registry containing symptomatic hereditary and wild-type ATTR patients and asymptomatic TTR mutation carriers that can support natural-history and outcome studies.

papers.title: Characterizing the High Disease Burden of Transthyretin Amyloidosis for Patients and Caregivers.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional observational study found substantial physical, functional, psychosocial, and economic burden in patients with ATTR amyloidosis, as well as marked burden in their caregivers. The paper also identifies liver transplantation, tafamidis, diflunisal, diuretics, and pacemakers as interventions for different ATTR manifestations, but treatment-effectiveness claims are largely based on cited prior studies rather than direct testing in this survey.
papers.why: This same-disease study provides patient and caregiver outcome instruments and associated ATTR amyloidosis burden data that can support clinical and natural-history assessments.

papers.title: Cardiac findings and events observed in an open-label clinical trial of tafamidis in patients with non-Val30Met and non-Val122Ile hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis.
papers.summary: In a 12-month, open-label phase 2 study of 21 patients with non-Val30Met and non-Val122Ile hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis, tafamidis was generally well tolerated and was associated with little short-term cardiac deterioration. Cardiac amyloid infiltration, biomarkers, electrocardiographic measures, and ventricular function were mostly stable, but progression occurred in some patients and the absence of a control group prevents attributing the observed stability to tafamidis.
papers.why: This clinical trial reports stabilization of non-Val30Met/non-Val122Ile TTR variants and cardiac outcomes in patients with hereditary ATTR amyloidosis.

papers.title: Survival After Transplantation in Patients With Mutations Other Than Val30Met: Extracts From the FAP World Transplant Registry.
papers.summary: In a registry cohort of 264 patients with hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis carrying non-Val30Met mutations, post-transplant survival varied markedly by mutation, baseline nutritional status, and presence of leptomeningeal disease. Liver transplantation was a viable option for selected mutations, whereas combined liver-heart transplantation was favored for certain cardiomyopathic mutations; mutation-specific evidence was limited by small cohorts.
papers.why: The international registry provides a substantial outcome dataset for liver transplantation across 57 TTR mutations, including long-term mutation-specific survival.

papers.title: Clinical Presentation, Diagnosis and Treatment of TTR Amyloidosis.
papers.summary: This review describes hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRm) as a genetically heterogeneous, multisystem disorder caused by amyloidogenic TTR variants and reviews its clinical manifestations, diagnostic methods, prognostic biomarkers, and disease-modifying therapies. It reports evidence for TTR tetramer stabilization, liver transplantation, and liver-directed gene-silencing approaches, while emphasizing genotype variability, diagnostic delay, organ-specific amyloid typing, and treatment limitations such as thrombocytopenia with inotersen and failure of the two gene-silencing drugs to suppress CNS or retinal TTR production.
papers.why: This disease-specific review identifies diagnostic strategies and reports recent disease-modifying gene-silencing approaches for hereditary ATTR amyloidosis.

papers.title: Temporal Trends of Wild-Type Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy in the Transthyretin Amyloidosis Outcomes Survey.
papers.summary: In a large international observational registry, wild-type transthyretin amyloidosis diagnoses and the use of bone scintigraphy increased substantially, while more patients were diagnosed at less advanced New York Heart Association functional class. Despite broader diagnostic use, the median delay from symptom onset to diagnosis remained prolonged and unchanged over the five most recent study years.
papers.why: Analyzes longitudinal THAOS data showing diagnostic trends and use of bone scintigraphy for cardiac ATTR amyloidosis.

papers.title: Sudomotor innervation in transthyretin amyloid neuropathy: Pathology and functional correlates.
papers.summary: In 28 patients with TTR Ala97Ser familial amyloid polyneuropathy, distal-leg skin biopsies demonstrated marked loss of PGP 9.5-positive and VIP-positive sweat-gland innervation, confirming structural and functional sudomotor denervation. The PGP 9.5-based sweat gland innervation index was associated with autonomic dysfunction, current disability, and shorter time to loss of ambulation, whereas the VIP-based index did not correlate with these clinical outcomes.
papers.why: Establishes quantitative skin-biopsy markers of sudomotor denervation that correlate with autonomic symptoms, disability and progression in TTR amyloid neuropathy.

papers.title: Ultrastructure in Transthyretin Amyloidosis: From Pathophysiology to Therapeutic Insights.
papers.summary: This review describes ATTR amyloidosis as a systemic disease caused by deposition of wild-type or variant transthyretin, with variant TTR misfolding, amyloid fibril formation, oligomer toxicity, microangiopathy, and tissue-specific organ dysfunction. It summarizes therapeutic approaches that reduce TTR production, stabilize TTR, or eliminate deposited TTR, including liver transplantation, tafamidis, diflunisal, patisiran, inotersen, and epigallocatechin-3-gallate.
papers.why: This same-disease review summarizes established transplantation, stabilizer, and RNA-silencing therapies and ultrastructural methods relevant to ATTRv amyloidosis.

papers.title: Multidisciplinary Approaches for Transthyretin Amyloidosis.
papers.summary: This review describes the diagnosis, mechanistic basis, and management of hereditary variant transthyretin amyloidosis, emphasizing neuropathy, cardiomyopathy, and systemic amyloid deposition. It reports evidence for TTR stabilizers, gene-silencing therapies, liver transplantation, tissue diagnostics, and noninvasive cardiac imaging, while noting important treatment limitations and uncertain interindividual response.
papers.why: The review describes clinically used imaging-based diagnostic pathways and multiple approved disease-modifying treatment classes for ATTR amyloidosis.

papers.title: Prognosis of Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis Without Heart Failure Symptoms.
papers.summary: In a retrospective international cohort of 118 patients with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy without heart failure symptoms, approximately one-third developed heart failure within a median 3.7 years, while other cardiac complications were also common. Treatment with transthyretin stabilizers was associated with improved survival and a nonsignificant trend toward delayed heart failure, but the retrospective design, selection bias, and limited sample preclude causal conclusions.
papers.why: This multicenter cohort establishes prognosis and symptom-free survival endpoints for ATTR cardiomyopathy and reports an association between TTR stabilizers and improved survival.

papers.title: Cardiac Troponin in Patients With Light Chain and Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis: <i>JACC: CardioOncology</i> State-of-the-Art Review.
papers.summary: This review finds that cardiac troponin, particularly high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T, is an established prognostic biomarker in ATTR cardiac amyloidosis and may support diagnostic assessment, risk staging, and treatment monitoring. Tafamidis stabilized NT-proBNP and hs-cTnT over time in ATTR cardiac amyloidosis, but prospective validation of troponin-based monitoring criteria remains limited.
papers.why: The review reports cardiac troponin as an established biomarker with diagnostic and prognostic applications in ATTR cardiac amyloidosis.

papers.title: Drug Discovery and Development in Rare Diseases: Taking a Closer Look at the Tafamidis Story.
papers.summary: This review describes how identifying tetramer dissociation as the rate-limiting step in transthyretin aggregation enabled rational development of the TTR kinetic stabilizer tafamidis. Clinical and real-world evidence supports tafamidis for hereditary ATTR polyneuropathy and wild-type or variant ATTR cardiomyopathy, although the pivotal polyneuropathy trial missed its coprimary endpoints and cardiomyopathy treatment remains limited by advanced disease and access-related challenges.
papers.why: This review documents tafamidis as an approved disease-modifying therapy for ATTR amyloidosis and summarizes reusable drug-development and trial-design methods.

papers.title: Assessment of cardiac amyloidosis with 99mTc-pyrophosphate (PYP) quantitative SPECT.
papers.summary: The study shows that 99mTc-PYP quantitative SPECT with phantom-derived, adjustable partial-volume correction can objectively distinguish ATTR cardiomyopathy from AL cardiac amyloidosis and other myocardial disorders. SUVmax tracked Perugini visual grades and showed strong intra- and inter-operator reproducibility, but validation was limited by only six ATTR-CM patients, camera-specific calibration, absence of prognostic data, and lack of repeat-scan testing.
papers.why: The study validates quantitative 99mTc-PYP SPECT with reproducible uptake thresholds for differentiating ATTR cardiac amyloidosis from AL amyloidosis and other cardiac disorders.

papers.title: Characteristics of Patients with Late- vs. Early-Onset Val30Met Transthyretin Amyloidosis from the Transthyretin Amyloidosis Outcomes Survey (THAOS).
papers.summary: This global observational THAOS analysis found that late-onset ATTRv Val30Met amyloidosis was common and was associated with longer diagnostic delays, more severe neurologic impairment and walking disability, and more prominent cardiac abnormalities than early-onset disease. The study also identifies amyloid fibril composition, deposition pattern, and age-related factors as reported or hypothesized determinants of phenotypic heterogeneity, but does not evaluate disease-modifying therapy.
papers.why: The large longitudinal THAOS analysis provides an ATTR patient registry and neurological and cardiac outcome measures for hereditary Val30Met disease.

papers.title: Characteristics and natural history of autonomic involvement in hereditary ATTR amyloidosis: a systematic review.
papers.summary: This systematic review finds that autonomic dysfunction is common, often early, and progressive in hereditary transthyretin-related amyloidosis, with its emergence and severity varying by TTR mutation and age at onset. Clinical studies reviewed here associate autonomic decline with neuropathy and functional disability, while questionnaires, autonomic tests, blood-pressure monitoring, and emerging biomarkers may help evaluate this component of disease progression.
papers.why: This systematic review identifies concrete clinical endpoints and surrogate measures for characterizing autonomic progression in hereditary ATTR amyloidosis.

papers.title: British Society of Echocardiography guideline for the transthoracic echocardiographic assessment of cardiac amyloidosis.
papers.summary: This guideline review finds that transthoracic echocardiography is useful for raising suspicion of cardiac amyloidosis, quantifying disease-related cardiac dysfunction, and estimating prognosis, but it cannot establish or subtype amyloidosis without confirmatory testing. In hereditary ATTR amyloidosis, echocardiographic strain, filling, ventricular wall, valve-regurgitation, and stroke-volume findings are clinically informative, particularly alongside cardiac MRI and bone scintigraphy.
papers.why: Provides a focused guideline and structured echocardiographic protocol for diagnosis, screening, prognosis, and cardiac assessment in transthyretin amyloidosis.

papers.title: 18F-flutemetamol positron emission tomography in cardiac amyloidosis.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 12 patients with cardiac amyloidosis, including three with hereditary ATTR cardiac amyloidosis, 18F-flutemetamol PET was positive in only two patients and had an overall sensitivity of 16.7%. Cardiac MRI abnormalities, including late gadolinium enhancement, prolonged global relaxation time, and increased extracellular volume, were more consistently observed than increased PET tracer uptake.
papers.why: The study directly evaluates 18F-flutemetamol imaging for detecting cardiac amyloidosis, including ATTR, and quantifies its diagnostic performance and limitations.

papers.title: Use of Drugs for ATTRv Amyloidosis in the Real World: How Therapy Is Changing Survival in a Non-Endemic Area.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 105 Sicilian patients with genetically confirmed hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis, disease-modifying treatment was associated with longer median survival than symptomatic treatment or no disease-specific therapy. Tafamidis was the most frequently used treatment, while the cohort also provides evidence on genetic testing, nerve biopsy, polyneuropathy staging, liver transplantation, patisiran, inotersen, and symptomatic management.
papers.why: The real-world cohort compares disease-modifying therapies in hereditary ATTR polyneuropathy and reports longer survival among treated patients.

papers.title: Quality of life assessment in amyloid transthyretin (ATTR) amyloidosis.
papers.summary: This review finds that phase 2 and phase 3 ATTR amyloidosis trials use heterogeneous generic, cardiac, and neurologic quality-of-life measures, but no instrument fully captures the disease’s phenotypic spectrum. It highlights the ongoing ITALY study, which is developing and validating separate patient-reported outcome measures for wild-type and variant ATTR amyloidosis.
papers.why: Identifies patient-reported and clinical outcome measures used in ATTR amyloidosis trials and describes development of disease-specific quality-of-life instruments.

papers.title: Five-Year Results With Patisiran for Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Polyneuropathy: A Randomized Clinical Trial With Open-Label Extension.
papers.summary: Five-year open-label follow-up found that patisiran produced modest but sustained clinical benefits in adults with hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy, including attenuation of deterioration in ambulation, neuropathy, nutritional status, quality of life, and disability. Earlier patisiran exposure was associated with better survival, while infusion-related reactions and other adverse events occurred without new long-term safety signals.
papers.why: Five-year randomized-trial extension data directly establish the long-term efficacy, safety, and clinically relevant outcomes of patisiran in hereditary ATTR polyneuropathy.

papers.title: Phenotypic expressions of hereditary Transthyretin Ala97Ser related Amyloidosis (ATTR) in Taiwanese.
papers.summary: This retrospective observational cohort of Taiwanese patients with hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis caused by the TTR Ala97Ser variant characterized a progressive course combining peripheral and autonomic neuropathy with cardiac involvement. The findings support early clinical suspicion, TTR DNA testing, and supportive electrophysiological and cardiographic evaluation even when tissue biopsy is negative.
papers.why: The cohort defines early clinical and cardiac manifestations that can accelerate recognition and monitoring of Ala97Ser hereditary ATTR amyloidosis.

papers.title: Hereditary transthyretin-related amyloidosis is frequent in polyneuropathy and cardiomyopathy of no obvious aetiology.
papers.summary: In a multicenter observational cohort of 5,141 patients with unexplained polyneuropathy, cardiomyopathy, or both, TTR sequencing identified a reportable heterozygous TTR variant in 1.1% of participants. TTR-positive patients had later age at onset and lower BMI, but no substantial differences in the frequency of 26 individual symptoms; the findings support routine TTR genetic testing in this risk population.
papers.why: Large multicenter study supports routine genetic screening in unexplained polyneuropathy and cardiomyopathy and reports a 1.1% diagnostic yield.

papers.title: Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis in Eight Chinese Families.
papers.summary: In nine Chinese patients from eight families with hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis, the study identified six TTR missense variants and documented variable polyneuropathy, autonomic dysfunction, cardiomyopathy, vitreous opacity, hearing loss, and macroglossia. Sural nerve biopsies frequently failed to demonstrate amyloid, whereas skin electron microscopy revealed capillary amyloid in one patient with a negative sural nerve biopsy, supporting broad TTR genetic testing in adult progressive neuropathies.
papers.why: The study provides molecular screening and tissue-based diagnostic approaches for suspected hereditary TTR amyloidosis, including mutation-negative biopsy findings.

papers.title: Clinical characteristics and prognosis of Chinese patients with hereditary transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 23 Chinese patients with hereditary transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, neuropathy predominated clinically while echocardiography revealed cardiac amyloidosis in every patient and identified symmetric left-ventricular hypertrophy and diastolic dysfunction. Prognosis was poor, and survival was better in patients with left-ventricular ejection fraction of at least 50% at diagnosis.
papers.why: This same-disease cohort establishes clinical recognition features and LVEF-based prognostic stratification for hereditary ATTR cardiac amyloidosis.

papers.title: CLEOPATTRA: A Research Study to Look at the Effects of Treatment With a Medicine Called Coramitug (NNC6019-0001) in People With Heart Failure Due to Transthyretin Amyloid (ATTR) Amyloidosis
papers.summary: This study will find out if a new medicine called NNC6019-0001 can help reduce the risk of heart-related death and illness in participants with a condition called transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), which affects the heart. Participants will either receive NNC6019-0001 or a placebo (a treatment with no active medicine), and which one they get is decided by chance. Everyone in the study will continue receiving their usual heart treatments as recommended by their doctor.

papers.title: HELIOS-A: A Study of Vutrisiran (ALN-TTRSC02) in Patients With Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis (hATTR Amyloidosis)
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of vutrisiran (ALN-TTRSC02) in participants with hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis (hATTR amyloidosis). Participants will receive vutrisiran subcutaneous (SC) injection once every 3 months (q3M) or the reference comparator patisiran intravenous (IV) injection once every 3 weeks (q3w) during the 18 month Treatment Period. This study will use the placebo arm of the APOLLO study (NCT01960348) as an external comparator for the primary and most other efficacy endpoints during the 18 Month Treatment Period. Following the 18 Month Tr

papers.title: TRITON-PN: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Nucresiran in Patients With Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Polyneuropathy
papers.summary:
The purpose of this study is to:

* Determine the efficacy of nucresiran in patients with hATTR-PN by evaluating the effect on neurologic impairment, quality of life, nutritional status, disability, and gait speed
* Demonstrate superiority of nucresiran compared to in-study vutrisiran with respect to serum transthyretin (TTR) levels

papers.title: An Extension of Study Fx-005 Evaluating Long-Term Safety And Clinical Outcomes Of Fx-1006A In Patients With Transthyretin Amyloid Polyneuropathy
papers.summary:
This study is designed to determine the long-term safety and tolerability of Fx-1006A as well as the effects of Fx-1006A on clinical outcomes in patients with ATTR-PN.

All patients who enroll in this extension study will receive once-daily oral 20 mg Fx-1006A for 12 months; therefore, patients randomized to placebo in Study Fx-005 will cross over to active drug (Fx-1006A 20 mg) during this study. However, patients and their families as well as clinical Investigators and their clinical site staff will remain blinded to the original Fx-005 treatment assignment. It is intended that there will be

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Acoramidis (AG10) in Subjects with Transthyretin Amyloid Polyneurophathy (ATTRibute-PN)
papers.summary: Phase 3 efficacy and safety of acoramidis in subjects with symptomatic Transthyretin Amyloid Polyneuropathy (ATTR-PN)

papers.title: The Effect Of Tafamidis For The Transthyretin Amyloid Polyneuropathy Patients With V30M Or Non-V30M Transthyretin
papers.summary: Tafamidis has been developed as an oral specific stabilizer of transthyretin tetramer.

papers.title: A Study to Characterize Adverse Events Occurring Within One Day of TEGSEDI Administration to Adult Participants With hATTR-PN
papers.summary: The objective of the study was to characterize adverse events (AEs) occurring within one day of TEGSEDI administration to adult participants with hATTR-PN overall and in individual participants with respect to time course of AE onset, vital sign changes, preventive measures, treatment required, risk factors, and subsequent adverse outcomes.

papers.title: EOSS-ATTR Study (eHealth Based Operative Support System in ATTR-CM)
papers.summary: Unicenter, proof-of-concept, prospective, randomised, controlled, open-label and blinded end-point adjudication trial to assess the effect on patient-reported outcomes measures (PROMs), patient-reported experience measures (PREMs) and clinical events of a mHealth-based comprehensive management program for patients with chronic heart failure (HF) due to transthyretin-associated amyloidosis (ATTR)-cardiomyopathy (CM) by means of remote daily telemonitoring of signs and symptoms and remote structured follow-up using videoconference.

papers.title: Virtual Reality Assisted Patient Empowerment: Diagnose ATTR-Amyloidosis And Start Treatment
papers.summary: ATTR amyloidosis is a serious condition with significant morbidity and mortality. In Germany, there are numerous unreported cases of untreated patients, and diagnosing and initiating treatment often requires multiple specialized tests. To address this, a study is being conducted to determine if virtual reality (VR)-based patient education can improve diagnosis rates, treatment initiation, and medication adherence compared to standard education methods.

papers.title: ENDEAVOUR: Phase 3 Multicenter Study of Revusiran (ALN-TTRSC) in Patients With Transthyretin (TTR) Mediated Familial Amyloidotic Cardiomyopathy (FAC)
papers.summary: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the safety and efficacy of revusiran (ALN-TTRSC) in patients with transthyretin (TTR) mediated Familial Amyloidotic Cardiomyopathy. Dosing has been discontinued; patients are being followed-up for safety.

papers.title: Spectrum of Peripheral and Autonomic Neuropathies in Patients With aTTRwt Amyloidosis and Response to Patisiran Therapy
papers.summary: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of patisiran in patients with wtATTR amyloidosis and symptomatic polyneuropathy by evaluating the effect on neurologic impairment and quality of life.

papers.title: APOLLO: The Study of an Investigational Drug, Patisiran (ALN-TTR02), for the Treatment of Transthyretin (TTR)-Mediated Amyloidosis
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of patisiran (ALN-TTR02) in patients with transthyretin (TTR) mediated amyloidosis. An open-label, single-arm, long-term follow-up extension study NCT02510261 (ALN-TTR02-006) was initiated to provide participants who completed this study with continued patisiran-LNP (lipid nanoparticle) treatment.

papers.title: The Study of an Investigational Drug, Revusiran (ALN-TTRSC), for the Treatment of Transthyretin (TTR)-Mediated Amyloidosis in Patients Whose Disease Has Continued to Worsen Following Liver Transplant
papers.summary: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of revusiran (ALN-TTRSC) in adults with transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (ATTR), whose disease has continued to worsen after liver transplantation. Dosing has been discontinued; patients are being followed-up for safety.

papers.title: A Study of PRX004 in Subjects With Amyloid Transthyretin (ATTR) Amyloidosis
papers.summary: A Phase 1, open-label study of intravenous (IV) PRX004 as a single agent in subjects with hereditary amyloid transthyretin (hATTR) amyloidosis. The study will consist of 3 phases and will enroll up to a total of 36 subjects. A 3+3 dose escalation component to determine the safety, tolerability, PK, PD, and MTD. An expansion component in anticipated PRX004 RP2D cohorts selected from the Dose Escalation Phase. An extended dosing component for eligible subjects from the Dose Escalation or Expansion phases.

papers.title: APOLLO-B: A Study to Evaluate Patisiran in Participants With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy (ATTR Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy)
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of patisiran in participants with ATTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy.

papers.title: A Research Study to Look at the Distribution and Effects of Coramitug on Amyloid Deposits in Heart Tissue Using PET/CT Imaging in People With ATTR Amyloidosis.
papers.summary: The study is conducted in participants with Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), a heart disease that occurs in people with the disease ATTR amyloidosis. The purpose of this study is to see how radioactively labelled coramitug is taken up by the heart after administration through an infusion (Cohort 1), and to understand the extent to which coramitug can be displaced by radioactively labelled coramitug (Cohort 2). In this study it will also be investigated how safe coramitug is and how well it is tolerated when it is used by participants with ATTR-CM. Coramitug is potentially a new

papers.title: Open Targets drugs acting on TTR
Cardiac Amyloidosis Treatment.
papers.summary: This review identifies TTR tetramer stabilization as an intervention strategy for ATTR cardiac amyloidosis by preventing transthyretin tetramer dissociation. Tafamidis has clinical evidence for reducing mortality and cardiovascular hospitalization in ATTR-CA, while diflunisal and acoramidis are TTR stabilizers with more limited or investigational evidence.

papers.title: Iodine atoms: a new molecular feature for the design of potent transthyretin fibrillogenesis inhibitors.
papers.summary: The study identifies iodine-containing diflunisal analogues, especially iododiflunisal, as potent transthyretin fibrillogenesis inhibitors that bind native TTR, stabilize its tetramer, and slow tetramer dissociation. Iododiflunisal more effectively prevented amyloid aggregate formation from the amyloidogenic TTRY78F variant and showed no significant metabolic dysfunction in TTRV30M transgenic mice, although further preclinical validation was required.

papers.title: Selective binding to transthyretin and tetramer stabilization in serum from patients with familial amyloidotic polyneuropathy by an iodinated diflunisal derivative.
papers.summary: The paper shows that two novel iodinated diflunisal derivatives preferentially bind transthyretin over albumin and thyroxine binding globulin in patient plasma and stabilize transthyretin tetramers.
