One derivative also efficiently inhibited transthyretin aggregation under the in vitro conditions, whereas diclofenac, flufenamic acid, and diflunisal did not comparably inhibit fibril formation.

papers.title: A substructure combination strategy to create potent and selective transthyretin kinetic stabilizers that prevent amyloidogenesis and cytotoxicity.
papers.summary: The study shows that selected stilbene and dihydrostilbene small molecules bind the native transthyretin tetramer, slow transthyretin tetramer dissociation, inhibit amyloid fibril formation, and largely rescue IMR-32 cells from wild-type and V30M transthyretin-induced cytotoxicity. The compounds were potent but had variable selectivity, because approximately half of the evaluated stabilizers bound the thyroid hormone receptor.

papers.title: The modulation of transthyretin tetramer stability by cysteine 10 adducts and the drug diflunisal. Direct analysis by fluorescence-detected analytical ultracentrifugation.
papers.summary: Using fluorescence-detected sedimentation velocity under nondenaturing conditions, the study found that S-sulfonation stabilizes recombinant transthyretin tetramers 7-fold, whereas S-cysteinylation enhances tetramer dissociation 2-fold. It also directly observed tetramer stabilization by diflunisal and demonstrated the sedimentation method in serum.

papers.title: Modulation of Amyloidogenic Protein Self-Assembly Using Tethered Small Molecules.
papers.summary: In the ΔN6 β2-microglobulin model of dialysis-related amyloidosis, site-specific covalent tethering to small-molecule fragments increased off-pathway tetramer populations and markedly reduced seeded amyloid fibril elongation. Disulfide-tethering screening, SV-AUC, thioflavin T fluorescence, X-ray crystallography, and NMR identified and structurally characterized these trapped tetramers, but the study did not examine transthyretin or transthyretin tetramer dissociation.

papers.title: Exploring Mechanisms of Inhibition of Amyloid Seeding of Transthyretin
papers.summary: The paper reports that ex-vivo TabFH2 binding inhibits further transthyretin amyloid seeding in a tissue-independent manner, whereas tetramer stabilization does not hinder seeding. These findings support peptide inhibitors of TTR amyloid seeding as a potential therapeutic approach, but no clinical efficacy is established.

papers.title: Novel diamine-scaffold based N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc)-siRNA conjugate: synthesis and in vivo activities.
papers.summary: The study developed diamine-scaffold GalNAc-conjugated siRNAs and showed liver-targeted delivery in mice, with 5′-end TG1 and 3′-end TG2 conjugates delivering TTR-targeting siRNA. A TG2 conjugate containing an additional phosphorothioate linkage produced 78% suppression of mouse TTR mRNA, while unmodified TG2 achieved 56% inhibition; these are preclinical gene-silencing results rather than treatment data in humans with amyloidosis.

papers.title: Two Birds with One Stone: A Novel Dithiomaleimide-Based GalNAc-siRNA Conjugate Enabling Good siRNA Delivery and Traceability.
papers.summary: The study developed a dithiomaleimide-containing tetra-antennary GalNAc–siRNA conjugate that delivered siRNA to primary mouse hepatocytes with uptake and TTR-silencing efficiency comparable to the GalNAc-L96 benchmark. Incorporating fluorescent dithiomaleimides into the scaffold enabled delivery tracking without an additional hydrophobic fluorophore, but the evidence is limited to in vitro cellular experiments.

papers.title: ESCRT-I complex enhances therapeutic efficacy of ASO drugs by regulating endosomal escape and glucose homeostasis.
papers.summary: In HepG2 and Huh7 liver-cell models, suppression of the ESCRT-I subunits VPS23 or VPS28 enhanced inotersen-mediated transthyretin gene silencing, primarily through reduced endosomal retention and altered intracellular glucose homeostasis. VPS23 suppression also enhanced patisiran-mediated TTR silencing, whereas MVB12A or VPS37A suppression had little or inconsistent effect, supporting a subunit-specific strategy for improving nucleic-acid-drug delivery in hepatocytes.

papers.title: Less Is More: Novel Hepatocyte-Targeted siRNA Conjugates for Treatment of Liver-Related Disorders.
papers.summary: The study shows that GalNAc-conjugated siRNAs can directly reduce the murine transthyretin transcript and serum TTR protein, demonstrating the delivery and knockdown mechanism relevant to transthyretin gene silencing. A 5′, 3′-sense conjugate, siRNA-24, showed greater in vivo activity and duration than a triantennary control, plausibly associated with increased stability in an acidified endosomal/lysosomal model, although the causal relationship was not confirmed.

papers.title: Tissue pharmacokinetics of antisense oligonucleotides.
papers.summary: This mouse study characterizes tissue pharmacokinetics and RNA knockdown for gapmer antisense oligonucleotides targeting Malat1 lncRNA. It shows that tissue exposure and knockdown depend strongly on administration route, ribose chemistry, and GalNAc conjugation, and that GalNAc conjugation improves liver delivery and liver-targeting potency without increasing liver RNA knockdown at the tested doses.

papers.title: A combinatorial approach for achieving CNS-selective RNAi.
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study shows that chemically modified, divalent siRNAs can silence APOE throughout the CNS after intracerebroventricular delivery, while liver-targeted GalNAc anti-siRNAs block or reverse the resulting off-target hepatic APOE silencing. In humanized APOE4 mice, combined delivery preserved greater than 95% brain APOE silencing while preventing measurable liver APOE reduction, without reported liver or kidney toxicity, although clinical translation would require more complex administration and safety studies.

papers.title: Impact of stereopure chimeric backbone chemistries on the potency and durability of gene silencing by RNA interference.
papers.summary: The paper shows that stereopure phosphorothioate and phosphoryl guanidine backbone chemistries can improve the potency and durability of GalNAc-siRNA-mediated RNA interference in mouse hepatocytes and mouse liver. Optimized designs enhanced Ttr and HSD17B13 mRNA silencing, increased antisense-strand exposure and Argonaute-2 loading, and did not significantly disrupt endogenous RNAi pathways or serum liver biomarkers in mice, although the benefit depended on linkage position, chirality, and nearby 2′-ribose chemistry.

papers.title: Effect of celastrol on toll‑like receptor 4‑mediated inflammatory response in free fatty acid‑induced HepG2 cells.
papers.summary: The study shows that celastrol reduces triglyceride accumulation and suppresses inflammatory signaling in free-fatty-acid-induced HepG2 cells, a cellular model of hepatic steatosis. TLR4 knockdown reduced lipid accumulation and inflammatory mediator expression, and combined TLR4 siRNA plus celastrol produced stronger suppression than either treatment alone; the paper does not study transthyretin or RNAi-mediated transthyretin messenger RNA degradation.

papers.title: Phosphorylation-specific status of RNAi triggers in pharmacokinetic and biodistribution analyses.
papers.summary: This study shows that ARC-520 delivers cholesterol-conjugated RNAi triggers to the liver and produces rapid 5΄-phosphorylation, RISC loading, and sustained HBV gene silencing in transiently HBV-transgenic mice. The peptide-nucleic acid hybridization assay with anion-exchange HPLC distinguishes non-phosphorylated, 5΄-phosphorylated, and metabolized guide strands and supports pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic analysis of RNAi-mediated messenger RNA degradation.

papers.title: SIRT1 regulates hepatic vldlr levels.
papers.summary: The paper shows that SIRT1 regulates hepatic VLDLR levels through HIF-1α-associated regulation and that SIRT1 activation with SRT1720 reduces tunicamycin-induced VLDLR elevation and hepatic steatosis. The study does not examine transthyretin, hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis, or RNAi-mediated transthyretin messenger RNA degradation.

papers.title: RNA-induced silencing complex-bound small interfering RNA is a determinant of RNA interference-mediated gene silencing in mice.
papers.summary: The study shows that the Argonaute2 (Ago2)-bound fraction of a lipid nanoparticle-formulated siRNA, rather than total siRNA accumulation in the liver, is closely associated with in vivo mRNA reduction and protein inhibition. Findings were demonstrated with luciferase siRNA and confirmed with an siRNA targeting endogenously expressed Sjögren syndrome antigen B (Ssb) mRNA, but the study did not examine transthyretin amyloidosis or the input disease mechanism directly.

papers.title: Poly(amine-co-ester) nanoparticles for effective Nogo-B knockdown in the liver.
papers.summary: This paper shows that solid poly(amine-co-ester) nanoparticles can deliver siRNA to hepatic cell populations and produce more than 60% suppression of the unrelated target Nogo-B in mouse liver for at least one week. It does not test transthyretin, TTR messenger RNA, or RNAi-mediated transthyretin messenger RNA degradation, so the platform is only an indirect delivery-system lead and is not mutation-specific evidence for the input disease.

papers.title: Serum amyloid P component prevents proteolysis of the amyloid fibrils of Alzheimer disease and systemic amyloidosis.
papers.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
papers.summary: The paper reports that serum amyloid P component (SAP) protects amyloid fibrils from proteolysis in Alzheimer disease, systemic amyloid A amyloidosis, and systemic monoclonal light chain amyloidosis. The authors propose that interfering with SAP binding to amyloid fibrils could promote regression of amyloid deposits, although no therapeutic intervention was tested.

papers.title: BRICHOS domain of Bri2 inhibits islet amyloid polypeptide (IAPP) fibril formation and toxicity in human beta cells.
papers.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
papers.summary: The study shows that the BRICHOS domain of Bri2 (ITM2B) acts as an antiamyloid chaperone: it inhibits IAPP amyloid fibril formation, redirects IAPP into amorphous aggregates, and reduces IAPP-associated toxicity in human beta cells, CHO cells, and Drosophila neurons. These findings provide a mechanistically transferable strategy for suppressing amyloid fibril formation, although the paper does not test transthyretin amyloidosis or transthyrerin itself.

papers.title: A small molecule Nec-1 directly induces amyloid clearance in the brains of aged APP/PS1 mice.
papers.summary: The study shows that necrostatin-1 (Nec-1) disassembles pre-existing amyloid-β oligomers, fibrils, and plaques and reduces amyloid-β-induced neuronal and microglial cell death in vitro and in aged APP/PS1 mice. These findings provide a preclinical amyloid-aggregate clearance strategy, but the paper does not test transthyretin amyloid fibrils or hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis, and reduced hippocampal plaques and unchanged cerebrospinal-fluid amyloid-β were not observed.

papers.title: Protein disulfide isomerase interacts with tau protein and inhibits its fibrillization.
papers.summary: The study shows that protein disulfide isomerase (PDI), primarily through its thioredoxin-like a-domain, binds Tau and inhibits Tau244–372 nucleation, elongation, and fibril accumulation under reducing in vitro conditions. It does not study transthyretin or transthyretin amyloid fibril formation, so the reported mechanism is not direct evidence of transfer to hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis.

papers.title: Nucleation seed size determines amyloid clearance and establishes a barrier to prion appearance in yeast.
papers.summary: This yeast study shows that the persistence and clearance of Sup35 amyloid after seed formation depend on both minimum seed size and Hsp104-mediated fragmentation; the larger-seeded [PSI+]Weak variant is more sensitive to fragmentation-mediated clearance than [PSI+]Strong. It also identifies Hsp104 availability and competition by Rnq1 amyloid as experimentally supported determinants of [PSI+] appearance, but it does not study transthyretin or explicitly examine transthyretin amyloid fibril formation.

papers.title: Truncation-Driven Lateral Association of α-Synuclein Hinders Amyloid Clearance by the Hsp70-Based Disaggregase.
papers.summary: The study shows that C-terminal truncation of α-synuclein promotes lateral association of fibrils and type B* oligomers, thereby reducing clearance by the Hsc70/DnaJB1/Apg2 human disaggregase. Recombinant truncation mutants and calpain-1-treated fibrils provide in vitro models for studying amyloid aggregate clearance failure caused by increased interfibril association.

unread.title: Mechanism of Action and Clinical Application of Tafamidis in Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis.
unread.why: This review describes tafamidis, an approved TTR-stabilizing therapy with clinical efficacy in hereditary ATTR neuropathy, alongside liver transplantation as a disease-modifying treatment.

unread.title: Updates on hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis polyneuropathy.
unread.why: This review summarizes multiple disease-modifying approaches and diagnostic strategies developed for hereditary ATTR amyloidosis, including gene-silencing and TTR-stabilizing technologies.

unread.title: Hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis: a model of medical progress for a fatal disease.
unread.why: This review documents established and emerging disease-modifying treatments for hereditary ATTR amyloidosis and their clinical roles in slowing disease progression.

unread.title: Transthyretin (ATTR) amyloidosis: clinical spectrum, molecular pathogenesis and disease-modifying treatments.
unread.why: This review reports clinically tested and developing treatments, transplantation, and genetic, biochemical, and immunohistochemical diagnostics for ATTR amyloidosis.

unread.title: Autonomic involvement in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis (hATTR amyloidosis).
unread.why: The review evaluates autonomic outcome measures used in hereditary ATTR trials and identifies instruments useful for diagnosis, prognosis, and tracking progression.

unread.title: Pittsburgh compound B positron emission tomography detects cardiomyopathy in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis patients with negative bone scintigraphy: a pilot study.
unread.why: This pilot study provides patient data showing that [11C]PiB PET/CT can detect cardiac ATTR amyloidosis when bone scintigraphy is negative, while its brain utility remains uncertain.

unread.title: Early Detection of Central Nervous System Involvement in ATTRv Using Multimodal MRI and Cognitive Assessments.
unread.why: The study demonstrates multimodal MRI and cognitive assessment as noninvasive methods for detecting early CNS involvement and white-matter damage in ATTRv polyneuropathy.

unread.title: Developing a phenotype risk score for TTR V142I to capture undiagnosed variant transthyretin amyloidosis in health systems.
unread.why: The study developed and validated an EHR-based phenotype risk score that identified undiagnosed TTR V142I carriers from routine clinical data.

unread.title: Progressive leptomeningeal involvement on gadolinium-enhanced FLAIR MRI in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with the V30M (p.V50M) mutation.
unread.why: Patient data indicate that leptomeningeal enhancement on Gd-FLAIR MRI is a frequent, sensitive, and progressive marker of CNS involvement in ATTR V30M amyloidosis.

unread.title: Italian Real-Life Experience of Patients with Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis Treated with Patisiran.
unread.why: Nine real-world cases report neurological, cardiovascular, safety, and quality-of-life outcomes with patisiran treatment in hereditary ATTR amyloidosis.

unread.title: Sixty years of experience with hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis: Insights from the Swedish transthyretin amyloidosis registry.
unread.why: The 1,055-patient national registry provides longitudinal clinical and treatment data, including survival observations for liver transplantation and disease-modifying drugs.

unread.title: Effectiveness and Utility of Genetic Testing in Establishing a Diagnosis of Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis.
unread.why: Large real-world testing programs demonstrate the diagnostic yield of targeted TTR sequencing in people with cardiac or neurologic suspicion or a relevant family history.

unread.title: Prognostic utility of the Perugini grading of 99mTc-DPD scintigraphy in transthyretin (ATTR) amyloidosis and its relationship with skeletal muscle and soft tissue amyloid.
unread.why: The study validates 99mTc-DPD scintigraphy and Perugini grading as a sensitive cardiac ATTR diagnostic and prognostic assessment method in a large same-disease cohort.

unread.title: Phenotypic characteristics of F64L, I68L, I107V, and S77Y ATTRv genotypes from the Transthyretin Amyloidosis Outcomes Survey (THAOS).
unread.why: The THAOS analysis provides longitudinal observational data and genotype-specific clinical phenotypes for four uncommon hereditary ATTR variants, supporting prognosis and comprehensive assessment.

unread.title: Advancing Transthyretin Amyloidosis Drug Development in an Evolving Treatment Landscape: Amyloidosis Forum Meeting Proceedings.
unread.why: This ATTR-specific forum report identifies reusable methods and data sources for overcoming confounding in clinical trials as effective therapies alter disease progression and natural history.

unread.title: Prevalence of hereditary transthyretin amyloid polyneuropathy in idiopathic progressive neuropathy in conurban areas.
unread.why: The study demonstrates that direct TTR sequencing detects hereditary ATTR cases missed by tissue biopsy and supports genetic screening in idiopathic progressive neuropathy.

unread.title: Glycosidic scaffold bearing multiple galloyl moieties from pomegranate disrupts transthyretin amyloids.
unread.why: The study experimentally shows that PGG disrupts preformed hereditary and wild-type TTR amyloid fibrils, reduces aggregation in a human-TTR C. elegans model, and acts on amyloid from patient cardiac tissue.

unread.title: Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis in Austria: Clinical, Genetic, and Demographic Insights from a Nationwide Cohort.
unread.why: The nationwide cohort provides a hereditary ATTR registry and genetic dataset while supporting cascade testing, multidisciplinary evaluation, and long-term monitoring.

unread.title: A review of Eplontersen use in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis.
unread.why: The review summarizes direct trial evidence that eplontersen lowers serum TTR and improves neuropathic impairment and quality of life in hereditary ATTR amyloidosis with polyneuropathy.

unread.title: Impact of Increasing Referral for 99mTc-DPD Scintigraphy on Prognosis Across the Phenotypic Spectrum of Restrictive Cardiomyopathy.
unread.why: This large ATTR-CM cohort provides clinical performance and prognostic data for 99mTc-DPD scintigraphy within a non-biopsy diagnostic pathway.

unread.title: The phenotypic landscape of p.Ala117Ser transthyretin amyloidosis: distinct clinical profiles and outcomes versus wild-type ATTR.
unread.why: The study supplies outcome and biomarker data showing how structured evaluation and genotype stratification can characterize hATTR and predict prognosis.

unread.title: Relationship between amyloid choroidopathy and neurological involvement severity scores in transthyretin amyloidosis.
unread.why: The ATTR cohort demonstrates that ICG-detected choroidal abnormalities can be quantified and related to validated neurological severity outcomes.

unread.title: Clinical and genetic features of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy in China: insights from case analysis and literature review.
unread.why: Genetically confirmed cases and a 70-case analysis support an integrated diagnostic strategy while documenting variable amyloid detection in sural nerve biopsies.

unread.title: Cardiac phenotype in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis: correlations between fibril types and 99mTc-DPD uptake.
unread.why: A 152-patient hATTR study directly compares fibril types, cardiac tracer uptake, clinical phenotype, troponin-T, and NT-proBNP.

unread.title: Effect of Eplontersen in Patients With Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Polyneuropathy Across Genetic Variants: An Exploratory Analysis From the NEURO-TTRansform Trial.
unread.why: Phase III exploratory analyses show that eplontersen lowers serum TTR and maintains or improves neuropathy and quality-of-life outcomes across TTR variants.

unread.title: Long-read Oxford Nanopore sequencing enables rapid, cost-effective, and comprehensive <i>TTR</i> genetic testing for hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis.
unread.why: The optimized ONT workflow was validated in 89 characterized samples and applied to 445 referrals with accurate detection, shorter turnaround, and lower cost.

unread.title: Transthyretin amyloid fibrils adopt distinct folds in the brain.
unread.why: Direct cryo-EM structures from two hereditary TTR variants reveal tissue- and variant-dependent fibril architectures and a conserved aggregation-associated segment.

unread.title: Val142Ile ATTR Cardiomyopathy: From Disease Progression to Clinical Stabilization With Vutrisiran.
unread.why: This case provides direct evidence that adding the RNA-silencing drug vutrisiran stabilized clinical disease and improved biomarkers after progression on tafamidis.

unread.title: The transthyretin amyloidoses: advances in therapy.
unread.why: Reviews tested and developing disease-modifying approaches that reduce TTR production, stabilize transthyretin, or dissolve amyloid in hereditary ATTR amyloidosis.

unread.title: Contributions of Animal Models to the Mechanisms and Therapies of Transthyretin Amyloidosis.
unread.why: Surveys disease models across multiple species and iPSC systems, including humanized knock-in mice that develop nerve amyloid and neuropathic manifestations.

unread.title: [Hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis].
unread.why: Identifies two established treatments for hereditary ATTR amyloidosis: liver transplantation and the TTR-stabilizing drug tafamidis.

unread.title: Evaluation of serum neurofilament light chain, GFAP, and peripherin as biomarkers in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis.
unread.why: Patient data show that serum NfL is elevated in symptomatic Val30Met ATTRv, differentiates carriers from controls, and tracks with greater neuropathy disability, while GFAP and PRPH lack diagnostic value.

unread.title: Not So Rare After All: Rethinking Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis
unread.why: Reports existing diagnostic, registry, and TTR-directed treatment resources for hereditary ATTR amyloidosis, although it is a review preprint rather than a primary treatment study.

unread.title: Neuropathy Assessment and Treatment Patterns in Patients with Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis
unread.why: The cohort shows that neuropathy coding alone is frequently unsupported and demonstrates how standardized clinical evidence and ancillary confirmation can inform treatment selection.

unread.title: Rationale and Design of ANTHOLOGY: An ATTR Amyloidosis Real-World Evidence Program Aiming to Address Gaps in Amyloidosis Care.
unread.why: Describes two multicountry real-world evidence studies designed to characterize ATTR treatment patterns, outcomes, diagnosis delays, resource use, and quality of life.

unread.title: Diagnostic & therapeutic challenges of presymptomatic hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis.
unread.why: Summarizes clinically available RNA-silencing therapies, monitoring frameworks, and NfL as a candidate marker for transition from presymptomatic to symptomatic ATTRv.

unread.title: Atypical gastrointestinal presentation of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis: a case report highlighting the diagnostic challenge.
unread.why: The case demonstrates tissue biopsy and targeted genetic testing as useful diagnostic solutions for atypical gastrointestinal and cardiac ATTR manifestations.

unread.title: Patisiran, an RNAi Therapeutic, for Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis.
unread.why: A phase 3 trial shows that patisiran significantly improves neuropathy in hereditary ATTR amyloidosis and reports validated clinical and quality-of-life endpoints.

unread.title: Nonbiopsy Diagnosis of Cardiac Transthyretin Amyloidosis.
unread.why: Multicenter data show that grade 2-3 myocardial tracer uptake plus absence of a monoclonal protein permits highly specific, reliable nonbiopsy diagnosis of cardiac ATTR amyloidosis.

unread.title: Expert Consensus Recommendations for the Suspicion and Diagnosis of Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis.
unread.why: This consensus report defines practical suspicion, diagnostic, and disease-characterization strategies directly applicable to cardiac manifestations of hereditary ATTR amyloidosis.

unread.title: Variant-sequence transthyretin (isoleucine 122) in late-onset cardiac amyloidosis in black Americans.
unread.why: Autopsy data show that cardiac amyloid assessment plus TTR genotyping can identify hereditary transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis in patients with otherwise unexplained heart disease.

unread.title: Clinical improvement and amyloid regression after liver transplantation in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis.
unread.why: The study provides direct clinical evidence that liver transplantation replaces variant TTR, improves disease manifestations, and can promote amyloid regression in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis.

unread.title: Cardiac amyloidosis: An update on pathophysiology, diagnosis, and treatment.
unread.why: Although a review, it summarizes clinically established diagnostic and treatment approaches for ATTR amyloidosis, including therapies directly relevant to mutant TTR disease.

unread.title: Prevalence and clinical phenotype of hereditary transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy in patients with increased left ventricular wall thickness.
unread.why: Prospective screening data support TTR genotyping in older patients with increased ventricular wall thickness and associated cardiac, neuropathic, or tendon phenotypes.

unread.title: Utility and limitations of 3,3-diphosphono-1,2-propanodicarboxylic acid scintigraphy in systemic amyloidosis.
unread.why: The study validates 99mTc-DPD scintigraphy as a sensitive cardiac imaging method for ATTR amyloidosis while defining its specificity limitations.

unread.title: Myocardial Edema and Prognosis in Amyloidosis.
unread.why: Cardiac MRI T2 mapping identifies myocardial edema and provides prognostic information in cardiac amyloidosis, including a cohort containing ATTR patients.

unread.title: Diagnostic pitfalls in sporadic transthyretin familial amyloid polyneuropathy (TTR-FAP).
unread.why: The study supports TTR DNA testing for progressive length-dependent polyneuropathy with autonomic dysfunction and quantifies biopsy and electrophysiologic diagnostic performance.

unread.title: Differential Myocyte Responses in Patients with Cardiac Transthyretin Amyloidosis and Light-Chain Amyloidosis: A Cardiac MR Imaging Study.
unread.why: Cardiac MRI extracellular-volume and cell-volume measurements distinguish amyloid-related extracellular expansion and myocyte abnormalities in mutant ATTR cardiac disease.

unread.title: Native state stabilization by NSAIDs inhibits transthyretin amyloidogenesis from the most common familial disease variants.
unread.why: In vitro testing shows that NSAIDs and a designed analog stabilize common disease-associated TTR tetramers and inhibit amyloid fibril formation.

unread.title: Liver transplantation and combined liver-heart transplantation in patients with familial amyloid polyneuropathy: a single-center experience.
unread.why: The study reports clinical use and survival outcomes of liver and combined liver-heart transplantation in familial amyloid polyneuropathy.

unread.title: Identification of transthyretin variants by sequential proteomic and genomic analysis.
unread.why: The study validates an integrated proteomic-genomic workflow that correctly identified known and novel TTR variants in a blinded patient and control set.

unread.title: Analysis of the TTR gene in the investigation of amyloidosis: A 25-year single UK center experience.
unread.why: A 25-year cohort of 4,459 patients demonstrates the diagnostic yield of TTR sequencing and identifies recurrent and novel pathogenic variants in ATTR.

unread.title: Frequencies and geographic distributions of genetic mutations in transthyretin- and non-transthyretin-related familial amyloidosis.
unread.why: Reports tested genetic testing methods and mutation frequency data for identifying hereditary ATTR amyloidosis.

unread.title: Genetic microheterogeneity of human transthyretin detected by IEF.
unread.why: Reports a validated electrophoretic method that detected essentially all tested amyloidogenic TTR mutations and characterized their destabilization.

unread.title: Genomic Screening for Pathogenic Transthyretin Variants Finds Evidence of Underdiagnosed Amyloid Cardiomyopathy From Health Records.
unread.why: Demonstrates large-scale genomic screening and EHR/clinical phenotype integration to identify underdiagnosed amyloid cardiomyopathy in TTR variant carriers.

unread.title: Association between hearing loss and hereditary ATTR amyloidosis.
unread.why: Provides tested audiological assessments showing frequent and often clinically unrecognized hearing loss in hereditary ATTR amyloidosis.

unread.title: Real-life experience with inotersen in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with late-onset phenotype: Data from an early-access program in Italy.
unread.why: Reports real-world long-term inotersen treatment outcomes and safety data in hereditary ATTR amyloidosis, including neurologic and autonomic endpoints.

unread.title: Transthyretin Kinetic Stabilizers for ATTR Amyloidosis: A Narrative Review of Mechanisms and Therapeutic Benefits.
unread.why: Reviews clinically developed TTR kinetic stabilizers and their mechanism, efficacy, and quality-of-life benefits in ATTR amyloidosis.

unread.title: Machine Learning for Early Diagnosis of ATTRv Amyloidosis in Non-Endemic Areas: A Multicenter Study from Italy.
unread.why: The multicenter study provides a validated clinical-feature and machine-learning workflow for identifying neuropathy patients who should undergo TTR genetic testing.

unread.title: Real-world outcomes in non-endemic hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy: a 20-year German single-referral centre experience.
unread.why: This long-term real-world study reports tafamidis efficacy, neurologic outcome measures, and NT-proBNP-based prognostic stratification in hereditary ATTR polyneuropathy.

unread.title: The "Wagshurst study": p.Val40Ile transthyretin gene variant causes late-onset cardiomyopathy.
unread.why: The cohort characterizes the cardiac phenotype of TTR Val40Ile with validated cardiac imaging, biomarkers, transplantation outcomes, and age-dependent penetrance data.

unread.title: Neurological involvement in Ile68Leu (p.Ile88Leu) ATTR amyloidosis: not only a cardiogenic mutation.
unread.why: Systematic neurological testing reveals previously unrecognized mixed phenotypes in Ile68Leu ATTR amyloidosis and identifies patients potentially eligible for gene-silencing therapy.

unread.title: Timing of Mortality Benefit in Outcomes Trials in Transthyretin Amyloidosis.
unread.why: The analysis establishes a reusable method for timing treatment effects and trial duration around the delayed mortality benefits observed with three ATTR-CM therapies.

unread.title: High prevalence of ATTR amyloidosis in endomyocardial biopsy-proven cardiac amyloidosis patients.
unread.why: The study provides a tissue-based workflow combining Congo red staining, TTR immunotyping, and genetic sequencing to distinguish ATTR from other cardiac amyloidoses.

unread.title: Cerebral Ischemic Events: An Overlooked Complication of Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis in Afro-Caribbean Patients.
unread.why: The cohort identifies CHA2DS2-VASc score as a readily available predictor of cerebral ischemic events in ATTR cardiac amyloidosis.

unread.title: Transthyretin variants impact blood-nerve barrier and neuroinflammation in amyloidotic neuropathy.
unread.why: Patient tissue, a mutant-TTR knock-in mouse, and an endothelial-cell model jointly provide mechanistic assays for blood-nerve-barrier disruption and neuroinflammation in ATTRv.

unread.title: Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis: Genetic Characterization of the <i>TTR</i> P.Val142Ile Variant in a Calabrian Kindred.
unread.why: The kindred study demonstrates a concrete TTR sequencing and family-screening workflow that identifies pathogenic p.Val142Ile carriers in a previously unrecognized population.

unread.title: Generation of two induced pluripotent stem cell lines from hereditary amyloidosis patients with polyneuropathy carrying heterozygous transthyretin (TTR) mutation.
unread.why: The study directly generated and characterized disease-relevant iPSC resources from hereditary ATTR polyneuropathy patients for mechanistic and modeling studies.

unread.title: Real-world treatment management in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis - an experience report and proposal for therapy switch decision criteria.
unread.why: The study analyzes real-world use of several disease-modifying ATTRv therapies and proposes clinically grounded criteria for switching treatments.

unread.title: Monitoring patients and asymptomatic carriers with hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis: regional protocol of Emilia-Romagna ATTR working group.
unread.why: The paper describes a concrete regional protocol and working-group resource designed to standardize ATTRv disease-progression monitoring and carrier follow-up.

unread.title: Role of ambulatory blood pressure monitoring as a non-invasive autonomic screening tool in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis.
unread.why: The study validates ABPM as a widely accessible noninvasive screening tool against quantitative autonomic testing in ATTRv patients and carriers.

unread.title: Deep Phenotyping of F64L Mutation in a Multicentric Cohort of Patisiran-Treated Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis Patients (Patisiranitaly).
unread.why: The multicenter Patisiranitaly study provides longitudinal mutation-specific clinical, cardiac, biomarker, and patient-reported outcome data relevant to treatment research in ATTRv.

unread.title: [Therapeutic Strategies for Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis].
unread.why: The review directly summarizes established disease-modifying treatment strategies for hereditary ATTR amyloidosis, including the approved gene-silencing drug vutrisiran.

unread.title: Amyloid fibril polymorphism in the heart of an ATTR amyloidosis patient with polyneuropathy attributed to the V122Δ variant.
unread.why: The study provides a structural method for characterizing patient-derived ATTR fibrils and links fibril polymorphism with phenotypic variation.

unread.title: Hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis incidentally diagnosed by video-associated lung surgery for lung cancer: A case report.
unread.why: The case demonstrates incidental tissue-based diagnosis of hereditary ATTR followed by initiation of disease-modifying vutrisiran therapy.

unread.title: Parallel Neurological and Cardiac Progression in Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis: An Integrated Clinical and Imaging Study.
unread.why: The study establishes sensitive cardiac and neurological measures for monitoring ATTRv progression and shows that cardiac abnormalities are detectable even in asymptomatic carriers.

unread.title: Long-term follow-up with magnetic resonance neurography in a patient with hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis treated with inotersen.
unread.why: The report evaluates an existing RNA-silencing therapy and a potentially reusable longitudinal neurography endpoint in hereditary ATTR amyloidosis.

unread.title: [<sup>18</sup>F]florbetapir PET for early detection of amyloidosis in patients with hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis polyneuropathy.
unread.why: The study reports an amyloid-specific PET method for early detection in patients with hereditary ATTR polyneuropathy.

unread.title: Endothelial glycocalyx disruption and early renal tubular injury in hereditary transthyretin Amyloidosis with dysautonomia.
unread.why: The title identifies measurable glycocalyx and renal tubular injury markers associated with early hereditary ATTR organ damage.

unread.title: Selective Cardiac Tc-99m DPD Retention With Markedly Reduced Extracardiac Uptake in Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis.
unread.why: Serial DPD imaging provides an existing cardiac amyloid assay and reveals an atypical myocardial-predominant uptake pattern in genetically confirmed hereditary ATTR.
